title: Inductors, cores and crystals
blurb: Explain piezoelectricity and the crystal's equivalent circuit, how core permeability, laminations and saturation affect inductors and transformers.

E6D01.why: Piezoelectric materials **generate a voltage when stressed** and **flex when a voltage is applied**.
E6D01.trap: It is a mechanical-electrical effect, not about light or EM waves.

E6D02.why: A crystal behaves as a **series RLC** (its mechanical resonance) with a **shunt capacitance** for the electrodes and strays.
E6D02.trap: Pure parallel RLC models miss the series resonance.

E6D03.why: Applying a voltage **mechanically deforms** the material; this is the piezoelectric effect.
E6D03.trap: Magnetic-field deformation is magnetostriction; light effects are photoelectric.

E6D04.why: Thin insulated layers keep **eddy currents** small, so less power is lost as heat in the core.
E6D04.trap: Layering is for loss, not cost or assembly.

E6D05.why: Ferrite's higher permeability means **fewer turns** for a given inductance.
E6D05.trap: Temperature stability is the powdered iron advantage.

E6D06.why: Inductance rises with the core's **permeability**: how well it carries magnetic flux.

E6D07.why: With the secondary open, the primary draws only the **magnetizing current** that creates the core flux.
E6D07.trap: It is not a load current, since none flows with no load.

E6D08.why: **Powdered iron** keeps its magnetic characteristics steadier with temperature than ferrite.
E6D08.trap: Ferrite has higher permeability, but drifts more with temperature.

E6D09.why: **Ferrite beads** are lossy at VHF/UHF, so they damp parasitic oscillations at transistor leads.
E6D09.trap: Beads, not steel-core toroids or filters, are the usual parasitic suppressor.

E6D10.why: On a toroid, **most of the magnetic field stays inside the core**, so it couples little to nearby parts.
E6D10.trap: Confinement reduces unwanted coupling; it does not add hysteresis or lower Q.

E6D11.why: Non-magnetic **brass** in a coil **lowers** inductance. Ferrite raises it; ceramic does little.
E6D11.trap: Ferrite is the classic inductance-raising core.

E6D12.why: Saturation happens at **excessive magnetic flux**: the core can't carry more.
E6D12.trap: Frequency and permeability choices do not cause saturation by themselves.
